findings.evidence: The first-release branch specifies `git log --first-parent --format='%h%x09%s' <to>`, omitting the body needed to recover merge PR titles. The breaking-footer scan at line 42 still uses `<from>..<to>`, although this branch has no start ref.
findings.fix: Resolve one revision expression: `<from>..<to>` normally and `<to>` for first releases. Use it in both log commands, retaining `--format='%h%x09%s%x09%b'` for commit collection. Give first-release empty-result messages wording that does not reference an undefined `<from>`.

findings.evidence: "If the tag resolves to the same commit as `HEAD`, rerun from `HEAD^` and use the older tag as the start." When HEAD is a tagged root commit, HEAD^ does not exist; the resulting invalid-object error matches neither documented describe-failure branch. Skipping a prerelease via `<tag>^` has the same boundary problem.
findings.fix: Verify that the parent commit exists before describing `HEAD^` or `<tag>^`. If it is unavailable, check whether the repository is shallow: stop and request a locally available start ref when shallow, otherwise enter the first-release branch.

findings.evidence: The Gotchas section states "A shallow CI checkout has no tags at all" and "Tags created on a release branch are not reachable from `main`." Both are overgeneralizations: shallow checkouts can contain tags, and merging release-branch history can make its tagged commits reachable from main.
findings.fix: Replace these claims with conditional facts: shallow CI checkouts may lack reachable version tags, so check shallow status after describe fails; release-branch tags are excluded only while their target commits remain unreachable from the selected endpoint.
